paper_title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream and propose RICoT (Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought), a prompting framework that works through the pages as a reader would: within a sliding window it reasons about each page and commits its boundary decision before moving on, and across windows it carries forward a compact record of what it has read, keeping per-call cost bounded. We also introduce FinancePSS-205, a benchmark of 205 real-world, de-identified financial page streams, to be released publicly. On FinancePSS-205, RICoT matches or outperforms pairwise and windowed prompting with the same backbone for each of three open-weight LLMs; on a TABME test subset, RICoT with GLM-5 reaches document F1 0.847 and boundary F1 0.915, above published zero-shot results. A 2B-parameter student, trained on a larger teacher's decisions with and without the page-level reasoning, performs comparably in both modes and comes within 0.05 document F1 of the strongest prompted model on FinancePSS-205.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Document-level information retrieval typically assumes predefined document boundaries. However, real-world page streamssequences of scanned or digital pagesoften bundle multiple documents into single file. Page Stream Segmentation (PSS) partitions these streams into their constituent documents (Figure 1), task critical for finance automation (AP/AR), where batched invoices, purchase 1 Figure 1: Page Stream Segmentation task. stream of six pages is segmented into four documents: two invoices (pages 12 and 3), delivery receipt (pages 45), and an email (page 6). Each document may span one or more consecutive pages. orders, and receipts are processed together; failing to segment them leads to merged field values, duplicated line items, and failed reconciliation. Traditional PSS relies on pairwise classification (Wiedemann and Heyer, 2018; Mungmeeprued et al., 2022; Heidenreich et al., 2024), deciding if page Pi starts new document based on Pi1. This paradigm suffers from two primary limitations: Contextual Isolation: Decisions often require long-range dependencies. For example, remittance advice on page 11 may only be identifiable as part of page 1 invoice via headers that pairwise classifier cannot see. Computational Redundancy: Encoding each page twiceonce as context and once as targetdoubles token costs without improving long-range reasoning. Conversely, full-stream processing falters as sequence length grows, since LLMs degrade in long contexts (Liu et al., 2024). Windowed classification (Pottanigari et al., 2026) is middle ground but is limited by fixed window boundaries. Our contributions are: The RICoT framework (Section 3): sliding-window PSS framework that combines interleaved per-page chain-of-thought reasoning within each window with recurrent state propagation across windowsa short reasoning history and an active-segment summary that maintain document-level coherence for arbitrarily long streams. distilled 2B student (Section 4): Qwen3.5-2B trained on Kimi-K2-Instructs RICoT outputs over finance-filtered subset of FinePDFs, with and without the page-level reasoning; the two modes perform comparably, and the student comes within 0.05 DocF1 of the strongest prompted model on FinancePSS-205. FinancePSS-205 (Section 5.1): new benchmark of 205 real-world, de-identified AP/AR page streams, to be released publicly with labels and evaluation scripts.1 Extensive ablations component (Sections 6.4 and 6.5) trace how each load-bearing element of RICoTpagewise interleaved reasoning, state propagation, the structured decision schema, and the deployment-time expand post-processing contributes to the frameworks accuracy. recurrent

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Page stream segmentation. PSS has progressed from visual CNNs classifying adjacent page pairs (Wiedemann and Heyer, 2018) through joint text-layout encoders (Mungmeeprued et al., 2022) to layout-feature embedding schemes (Drumond et al., 2023) and efficient image-only pipelines (Braz et al., 2021) on the Tobacco800 benchmark (Lewis et al., 2006; University of California, San Francisco, 2007; Agam et al., 2006). Heidenreich et al. (2024) adapt the paradigm to LLMs by prompting instruction-tuned models on adjacent page pairs and obtain the strongest zeroshot decoder baseline on TABME prior to our work; Heidenreich et al. (2025) extend the LLM treatment with new metrics and stronger fine-tuned baselines. PSS has also been formalized in adjacent media, e.g. multimodal Transformers on comic-book page streams (Serra Ortega et al., 2025), and real-world open benchmarks of Dutch government streams have been released (van Heusden et al., 2022, 2024). common thread across this prior work is the pairwise assumption: boundary decisions are made independently for each page given only the immediately preceding page, which limits context to the local pair. Concurrent MSBD (Pottanigari et al., 2026) predicts all boundaries of window in one call (the design of our Windowed baseline) and degrades at larger windows; generation-based segmenters (Inan et al., 2022; Li et al., 2026) are trained and read the full input. RICoT is zero-shot, keeps windows bounded, reasons per page, and carries state across windows. Commercial documentAI services, such as LandingAIs Agentic Document Extraction,2 Reducto,3 and LlamaIndexs LlamaParse,4 also offer document splitting, but do not publish their methods, so they cannot serve as reproducible baselines. Interleaved chain-of-thought reasoning. Chainof-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022) elicits intermediate reasoning steps before the final answer. The closest precedent for the mechanism we use is ReAct (Yao et al., 2023), which interleaves thought and action steps for agentic tasks; RICoT adapts the same interleaving principle to sequential classification, alternating per-page reasoning and per-page decision within window in one call, avoiding the per-page cost of multi-call agentic loop. Interleaved reasoning has recently been explored as training paradigm for LLMs (Xie et al., 2025); our contribution is at inference time, integrated with windowed processing and recurrent state for multipage sequential classification. Long-context state propagation. Long-context use is limited by the lost-in-the-middle effect (Liu et al., 2024) and by the cost of extending context windows. Architectural mitigations (Beltagy et al., 2020; Zaheer et al., 2020) and recursive decomposition (Zhang et al., 2025) change the underlying inference procedure; explicit memory-management approaches such as MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023) pass state across turns through structured sum1The dataset, evaluation code, prompt templates, and the additional materials referenced throughout this paper (the public release) are not yet public; URL will be added in future version of this preprint. 2https://docs.landing.ai/ade/ade-split 3https://docs.reducto.ai/api-reference/split 4https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/ split/getting_started/; all accessed October 2026. 2 maries. RICoT shares the explicit-state philosophy, instantiated for PSS as recurrent active-segment summary plus short reasoning history carried across overlapping windows.

sections.title: 3 RICoT Framework
sections.content: 3.1 Task definition Let = (x1, . . . , xN ) be page stream of pages, each represented by OCR-extracted text and layout features. PSS maps to binary boundary labels = (y1, . . . , yN ) with yi = 1 iff page xi starts new document; by convention y1 = 1. The labels induce partitioning into contiguous documents {D1, . . . , DK} where Dk = (xsk , . . . , xek ) and {s1 < < sK} = {i yi = 1}. 3.2 Sliding windows and the two-axis decision RICoT (Figure 2) processes with token-budgeted windows. Each window Wc is packed greedily with consecutive pages until the running token count would exceed budget or page cap wmax is reached, with one-page overlap into the previous window.5 This adapts window size to page densityshort pages pack densely up to wmax, long pages truncate earlyso context utilization is consistent across stream geometries. Two-axis decision. For each page in the window the model emits di = (yi, zi, ℓi, gi, ci), (1) where the segment axis yi {S, C} marks new segment (S) or continuation (C); on continuations, the sub-document axis zi {D, } optionally marks nested document instance (e.g. an invoice inside statement of account). ℓi is documentclass label, gi grounding fingerprint (page identifier + short evidence quote), and ci categorical confidence (HIGH(cid:55)9, MOD(cid:55)6, LOW(cid:55)3). ℓi is emitted only on decisions, so each segment has one label. Keeping segment-start and subdocument-start as separate axes at decision time preserves both signals for downstream control (Section 3.4). 3.3 Interleaved reasoning and recurrent state Within window, RICoT generates per-page reasoning (<think>) interleaved with the per-page 5We use = 3600 tokens, wmax = 6, = 1 across all experiments; values were fixed priori, not tuned. decision (<decision>) before moving to the next page. We refer to this as pagewise thinking (PwT); the alternative of emitting one block of reasoning followed by all decisions is the windowed thinking variant we ablate in Section 6.4. Interleaving grounds each decision in evidence local to its target page. Two recurrent state objects, (H(c), A(c)), are propagated across windows. H(c) is an anchored recency window: up to the k=6 most recent thoughtdecision pairs, always preserving the two decisions that opened the active segment (joined by an elision marker once they age out). A(c) describes the currently open segment in two parts: (i) deterministic metadata (s, ℓs, PAGES-COVERED) derived by walking back to the most recent decision, and (ii) model- <active_segment_carry_forward> emitted block κ(c) summarizing anticipated content and progress for the next window. The stream is wrapped with <stream>/</stream> tags so the model suppresses κ on the terminal window where no successor exists. Each page is decided in the first window containing it; later emissions for the overlap page are ignored. worked example is in Appendix F. Robust decoding. decision cache stores the most recent valid di per page. After parsing, any missing, malformed, or duplicate page is filled from first; if the page will recur in the next overlapping window the correction is deferred; remaining gaps are repaired by correction call, and finally by rule-based fallbacks (continuation by default, low-confidence UNKNOWN otherwise). The full procedure is summarized in Algorithm 1 (Appendix U). 3.4 Expand: deployment-time controllability Because the two-axis decision keeps sub-document starts as separate signal even when their parent segment is open, downstream consumers can re-threshold what counts as segment without re-running inference. We use this for one specific operating choice on FinancePSS205, which we call expand: when predicted sub-document of priority class (invoice, statement, purchase_order, packing_slip, commercial_invoice, bill_of_lading, packing_list) appears inside parent segment, the sub-documents start is promoted to true segment start in post-processing. The priority 3 on 100K Stage-1 documents labeled by an LLM judge for finance vs. non-finance. The combined filter yields 12.3M finance documents (100B tokens). Lexicon tiers, classifier details, and classification threshold tuning are in Appendix S. From this pool we sampled 300K documents. Because FinePDFs lacks page markers, we re-fetch each PDF via its Common Crawl URL and re-OCR it per page, using FinePDFs per-page language list to verify page-count alignment and drop unsupported scripts; 150,448 documents (50%) survive (Appendix P). samples We then ran RICoT with the teacher model (Kimi-K2-Instruct (Kimi Team, 2025)) over the 150,448 documents, producing 467,229 (each chunk is one chunk-level sliding-window span with the teachers interleaved reasoning, per-page decisions, and active_segment_carry_forward summary). Only 20,959 (13.9%) source documents contain the remaining 86% two or more segments; are self-contained single-segment documents, reflecting FinePDFs web-crawled provenance. Chunk selection. We keep every multi-segment file and every special chunk in it (containing or immediately preceding segment start, or ending the file), subsampling other chunks up to cap. Singlesegment files are downsampled within embedding clusters of the teachers free-form class labels, and truncated or single-page documents are dropped. The final corpus has 46,791 documents (20,959 multi-segment, 25,832 single-segment); caps will be included in the public release. 4.2 Training with and without page-level reasoning Each training sample is triple (SYS, CTX, OUT) system instruction, stream context, chunk output always rewritten together so the schema declared, carried, and produced agree. With probability 0.40 per chunk, the sample is rendered without page-level reasoning: the per-page <think> blocks are removed and the instruction no longer mentions reasoning, so the target is the teachers decisions alone; otherwise it keeps the teachers interleaved reasoning and decisions. One student thus serves both modes at deployment: with reasoning (Q3.5-2B,PwT) and decisions only (Q3.5-2B; Section 5.2). worked example of each will be included in the public release (Appendix R). For operational convenience only, some samples Figure 2: RICoT architecture. Window Wc processes its pages with interleaved per-page reasoning and decisions, receiving reasoning history H(c) and active-segment summary A(c) from preceding windows. Recurrent state and the per-page two-axis decision (segment + sub-document) extend effective context beyond the window boundary while keeping per-window inference cost bounded. list is taken from the document ontology of the AP/AR workflows the data come from and was fixed before any FinancePSS evaluation; expand uses no re-inference and no gold labels. We report its effect alongside the no-expand variant throughout Section 6 so its contribution is visible rather than absorbed into the headline number.

sections.title: 4 Distilling RICoT into a Small Model
sections.content: A small model running the same framework is more attractive to deploy than large prompted one, so we distill RICoT into 2B student: larger teacher LLM runs RICoT over training corpus, and the student learns to produce the teachers per-page decisions both with and without the accompanying page-level reasoning. 4.1 Training corpus from FinePDFs We construct training data from FinePDFs (Kydlíˇcek et al., 2025), publicly available PDFsourced corpus (3T tokens, 475M documents). We restrict to the English subset (206M documents) and isolate finance content through twostage filter: Stage 1 is high-recall keyword pass over tiered finance lexicon, and Stage 2 is an XGBoost classifier over TF-IDF features trained 4 also omit optional decision fields (e.g., document class, confidence, grounding) or the carry-forward progress field, so that one student accepts reduced or full schemas without retraining; yi is never removed, and we claim no accuracy contribution for this variation (Appendix O). 4.3 Training setup We fine-tune Qwen-3.5-2B (Qwen Team, 2026) with QLoRA (Dettmers et al., 2023) of rank 32 (α=64, dropout 0, target modules: all linear projections) for 1 epoch on the 46,791-document training corpus, with 1,800 samples held out for validation. We use cosine learning-rate schedule (8105, 8% warmup), AdamW-8bit, bf16 with gradient checkpointing, effective batch size 16 (perdevice 8, grad-accumulation 2). Training took 44 hours on 4A100 80GB. The full hyperparameter set is in Appendix Q. We report single training run; we did not sweep the sampling probabilities of Section 4.2 or the LoRA rank.

sections.title: 5 Experimental Setup
sections.content: 5.1 Datasets We evaluate on three benchmarks spanning different domains and complexity levels  (Table 1)  . TABME (Mungmeeprued et al., 2022). large synthetic page-stream benchmark built from the Truth Tobacco Industry Documents archive, in which 44,769 source PDFs were concatenated into folders mimicking real folder length and type distributions. Each source PDF forms one groundtruth segment, so TABME provides large, reproducible test of file-level segmentation. Inference cost on the full 5,000-stream test set is substantial, so we run prompting experiments on fixed random subset of 250 streams (TABME-250; stream IDs in Appendix G); our distilled model is additionally evaluated on the full 5,000-stream test set, where numbers track the subset closely (DocF1 0.756 vs. 0.770 on , PwT; Section 6.1). Tobacco800 (Lewis et al., 2006; University of California, San Francisco, 2007; Agam et al., 2006). standard PSS benchmark from the same archive, containing scanned letters, memos, and reports. Following Wiedemann and Heyer (2020) and Mungmeeprued et al. It is near ceiling and serves as reference rather than discriminating benchmark. FinancePSS-205 (new). 205 real-world page streams from production AP/AR workflows, mixing invoices, remittance advice, purchase orders, delivery receipts, statements, and email, with typical finance bundling (invoiceremittance pairs, PO invoice matches, invoices nested in statements). Each stream is one file exactly as received, so boundaries between related same-vendor documents must be inferred from content. new document starts wherever page begins document with its own transactional identity; labels were produced by the research team (no inter-annotator agreement study; see Limitations). We will release the de-identified page-level, spatially-aware text (the exact model input) with labels under CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial research use) and the evaluation scripts under Apache-2.0; the dataset card and trivial baselines are in Appendix A. We use only the test partitions of the public datasets; no training data from any benchmark is used in this work. 5.2 Models Prompted LLMs. GLM-4.7-flash (GLM Team et al., 2025) is the 30B small variant of the GLM4.7 family, our small-model prompting baseline roughly 15 the size of our distilled student; GLM-4.7 (GLM Team et al., 2025) is the full GLM-4.7 model; GLM-5 (GLM-5 Team, 2026) is 744B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model released under the MIT license by Z.ai; Claude Haiku 4.5 (Anthropic, 2025) is included as nonGLM frontier prompted-model point of comparison. By default we run RICoT with each models internal extended thinking off (Section 6.4). Distilled student. Qwen-3.5-2B (Qwen Team, 2026) distilled from Kimi-K2-Instruct (Kimi Team, 2025) as described in Section 4; the base model prompted with RICoT without fine-tuning is reported as control. Table labels. G4.7-F for GLM-4.7-flash, G4.7 for GLM-4.7, G5 for GLM-5, C-H4.5 for Claude Haiku 4.5, and Q3.5-2B for the Qwen-3.5-2B base model. The distilled-student variants are denoted Q3.5-2B (no pagewise thinking) and Q3.52B,PwT (with pagewise thinking). 5.3 Evaluation metrics We report five metrics spanning page, segment, and stream granularities. PageF1 (Heidenreich et al., 2025, 2024) is page-level boundary-classification F1. B-F1 (Pottanigari et al., 2026) is the same F1 over adjacent-page decisions only, excluding each streams first page. DocF1 (Heidenreich et al., 2024, 2025) is F1 over documents, each represented as the tuple of its page indices; true positive is an exact tuple match. All F1 scores are micro-averaged over streams. MNDDµ (perstream mean of Minimum Number of Drag-andDrops) is user-centric metric counting the minimum drag-and-drop operations needed to reconcile prediction with the ground truth in foldermanagement UI; lower is better. STP% (StraightThrough Pass) is the percentage of streams with zero boundary errors. All metrics are computed on the segment axis only and ignore class labels; the sub-document axis enters only through the withexpand rows (Section 3.4). 5.4 Baselines Baselines are re-run on our infrastructure with the same backbones as RICoT. Pairwise. Each adjacent page pair (pi1, pi) is classified independently for whether pi starts new document (Heidenreich et al., 2024, 2025); window size w=2, overlap o=1. Internal extended thinking enabled (its strongest configuration per Section 6.4). Windowed. fixed-size window of w=5 pages is shown to the LLM with single decision prompt asking for boundary labels across the window; windows overlap by o=1. Internal extended thinking enabled. The same single-call, multi-boundary design was proposed concurrently as MSBD (Pottanigari et al., 2026). 5.5 Implementation details The RICoT sliding window is sized by constant token budget (B=3600), per-window page cap (wmax=6), and one-page overlap (o=1); these were fixed priori and held constant across all experiments (sweep in Appendix C). Pages whose tokenized length exceeds fixed per-page threshold are truncated using head-and-tail rule (first 500 + last 300 tokens, with an explicit truncation marker between), since segmentation signal concentrates at document openings and closings. All inference uses temperature 0.001 (top-p 1) for both prompting and the distilled model. The inference configuration is described in Appendix T; structural prompt templates will be included in the public release. Prompted results are single runs; distilled-model FinancePSS and Tobacco800 numbers are means of 5 inference runs. Run-to-run variability and confidence intervals are in Appendix B.

The strongest prompted model (GLM-5) reaches DocF1 0.967 on Tobacco800 and 0.847 on TABME-250, and the strongest prompted-model FinancePSS configuration (GLM4.7) reaches 0.832 with expand. The distilled 2B model (Qwen-3.5-2B,PwT) reaches 0.785 on FinancePSS-205 and 0.770 on the full 5,000stream TABME test set without exposure to TABME training data. Its gap to the strongest prompted model is 0.047 DocF1 on FinancePSS205, 0.040 on Tobacco800, and 0.091 on TABME250 (same streams). The same base Qwen-3.52B prompted with RICoT but without fine-tuning reaches only 0.445 / 0.396 / 0.281 on the three datasets, isolating the contribution of distillation from base-model capacity and framework prompts. The two student modes perform comparably (0.785 vs. 0.773 on FinancePSS-205, with overlapping intervals in Appendix B; 0.770 vs. 0.774 on full TABME), so page-level reasoning can be skipped 6 at inference. 6.2 Comparison to prior published TABME baselines Table 3 compares RICoT with published TABME results (Heidenreich et al., 2024, 2025; Pottanigari et al., 2026). These span different test sets and OCR versions (table footnotes) and are indicative only. RICoT with GLM-5 (DocF1 0.847) beats the strongest published zero-shot decoder (GPT4o-ZS) by +0.144 DocF1 and +32 STP points; the distilled 2B model on the full test set (0.770) beats the XGBoost and DiT baselines of Heidenreich et al. (2024) and GPT-4o-ZS by +0.067. On boundary F1, we list for each model of Pottanigari et al. (2026) its best result across all their methods (PC, BD, MSBD), window sizes, and inputs: 0.866 (Claude Haiku 4.5), 0.887 (Gemini 3.1 FlashLite), and 0.876 (GPT-5.4-mini). RICoT, using text only, exceeds all of them: GLM-5 reaches 0.915 and Claude Haiku 4.5 0.901 (+0.035 over the same models best), and even the 2B students (0.890, 0.887) match or exceed them. None of our models approaches the fine-tuned LLMs (Phi3-mini, Mistral-7B) trained on TABMEs training split; the gap reflects both TABMEs file-level segment granularity and genuine errors of our models (Section 6.6). 6.3 RICoT vs. pairwise and windowed paradigms Table 4 reports DocF1 head-to-head against pairwise and windowed LLM-PSS baselines on all three datasets for the GLM family, with every method run on the same backbone (Tobacco800 has only one stream, but the single-stream DocF1 still differentiates configurations). On FinancePSS, RICoT is the best configuration for every model, by +0.154, +0.069, and +0.057 over the best baseline (GLM-4.7-flash, GLM-4.7, GLM-5). Without expand the margins are +0.133 and +0.032 and tie on GLM-5 (Section 6.6). Context length does not explain the gain: in control that keeps pairwise decisions but shows symmetric 5-page context (GLM-4.7-flash, 5 runs; Appendix D), pairwise rises from 0.506 to 0.651, yet RICoT still leads it by +0.111 (+0.090 without expand) with 2.15 vs. 7.6 calls per stream. On the nearceiling Tobacco800, RICoT wins for GLM-4.7 and GLM-5. On TABME-250, RICoT leads for GLM4.7 (+0.052) and GLM-5 (+0.092), while for the small GLM-4.7-flash, pairwise classification with internal thinking is stronger (0.771 vs. 0.683), mirroring its Tobacco800 result. 6.4 Pagewise vs. internal extended thinking Do RICoTs gains overlap with models internal extended thinking? We run 22 ablation on GLM4.7-flash crossing pagewise interleaved thinking with internal extended thinking across all three datasets  (Table 5)  . Pagewise yields positive DocF1 delta on every dataset; internal-thinking alone is positive only on FinancePSS and neutralto-negative elsewhere; the two are roughly additive when combined. Per-page output-token costs differ by an order of magnitude: on FinancePSS-flash, pagewise adds 60 output tokens to gain +0.074 DocF1, while internal thinking adds 650 tokens for +0.028. The per-channel cost breakdown is in Appendix J. We therefore default to internalthinking-off for all RICoT runs in this paper. 6.5 Component ablations Table 6 ablates each load-bearing component of RICoT on FinancePSS-205 across the three prompted GLM models by removing one component at time and re-running. Pagewise thinking is the largest single contributor on all three models (0.048 to 0.088 DocF1). Context propagation (reasoning history H(c) and active-segment summary A(c)) matters most for GLM-5 (0.048) and on long streams (Appendix E). Grounding is reliably positive for GLM-4.7-flash and GLM-5. Removing only the model-emitted carry-forward block is mixed, so the state-propagation story rests on the reasoning history; Appendix marks which deltas exceed run-to-run noise. Expand contributes +0.021 to +0.057. Per-dataset full ablation tables, including TABME and Tobacco800, are in Appendices K, L, and M. 6.6 Discussion Segment granularity on TABME. Run-to-run variability was measured with five repeats on GLM-4.7flash (Appendix B) and assumed to transfer to the other models, whose results are single runs; the student was trained once, and the effect of omitting optional decision fields during training was not isolated. Model coverage spans one model family at three scales plus one non-GLM model. The framework assumes that the first page of stream begins document and treats each page image as one logical unit, with no granularity for multiple pages combined into single scan. It relies on sequential continuity and cannot reassociate noncontiguous or interleaved pages into one document entity. Finally, recurrent state propagation makes within-stream processing strictly causal: multiple streams can be processed in parallel, but single long stream must be processed sequentially.

sections.title: Ethical Considerations
sections.content: The FinancePSS dataset was collected from production workflows under the data-handling agreements in force at the time and pseudonymised: personal names, addresses, contact details, and account numbers were consistently replaced with typeand length-consistent synthetic values, preserving document structure. The planned release will contain only this de-identified text (no page images), which was audited for retained identifiers (Appendix A), and will be licensed for noncommercial research use (CC BY-NC 4.0) under terms of use that prohibit re-identification; because free-text pseudonymisation cannot fully exclude re-identification, we treat the release as pseudonymised rather than anonymous. No human annotators beyond the research team were employed for dataset labeling. AI writing assistance was used for portions of manuscript drafting; all scientific content, experimental design, results, and conclusions are entirely the authors own.

sections.title: E Long Streams and Error Propagation
sections.content: Depth-stratified state propagation. On the 17 longest FinancePSS streams, restricting to deep pages (windows 5), full RICoT outperforms the no-context-propagation ablation by +0.178 DocF1 (GLM-5) and +0.131 (GLM-4.7), while the effect is negative for GLM-4.7-flash. Recurrent state therefore matters most where it is exercised (long streams) and for models with the capacity to use it; on short streams, which fit in one or two windows, it has little to act on. Error cascading. Mapping boundary errors to windows shows local persistence rather than systematic corruption: the next-window error rate is 5071% after an erroneous window versus 512% after correct one, yet 5469% of streams with an early error later produce an error-free window (median error run: 2 windows). This analysis is observational; causal estimate would require replay with corrected state.

We analyse the false boundaries (FPs) of Q3.5-2B (RICoT, no pagewise thinking) on the full 5,000-stream test set, scoring sub-document starts as continuations as in all our metrics (Section 5.3): precision 0.836, recall 0.951, B-F1 0.890, 9,331 FPs. We sampled 100 FPs: 45 at random (one per stream) and 55 as one error site per source file, from files not already sampled; they cover 98 distinct (file, page) sites. Each was judged by hand from the OCR text, and 25 of them, including every A1 site, were also checked against the page images; this changed one label (a magazine letters page first judged to come from another issue was the next page of the same issue). Categories. A1: genuine top-level document begins inside one source file (e.g. two separate funding records filed together); TABMEs file-level label merges them. A2: genuine nested document (envelope, enclosure, attachment, fax payload) that the model emitted as top-level start. In our framework the correct output is sub-document start, which the metric scores as continuation, so A2 is model error: the right document at the wrong level. B: no document starts here; the page continues the same document. C: ambiguous (archive slip sheets, near-empty pages, unreadable OCR). sections.title: P Training Corpus Attrition Breakdown
sections.content: Table 19 summarizes the per-stage attrition of the FinePDFs-derived training corpus. Of the 300K candidate documents sampled from the 12.3Mdocument finance subset, roughly 50% survive download and language-alignment filtering. The main attrition stages are: failed Common Crawl fetch (cache miss / dead URL), page-count mismatch between the downloaded PDF and FinePDFs metadata (indicating unreliable OCR alignment), and detection of pages in scripts unsupported by our OCR model. The surviving 150,448 documents feed into teacher labeling. Precision: bf16; gradient checkpointing on. Hardware: 4NVIDIA A100 80GB; wallclock 44 hours. Worked Training-Sample Example complete example showing the same source chunk rendered into training sample (i) with all schema fields present and pagewise reasoning emitted, (ii) without page-level reasoning (decisions only), and (iii) decisions only, with several optional decision fields also omitted, will be included in the public release. FinePDFs Finance-Filter Classifier The Stage 1 finance lexicon contains three tiers of keyword patterns of increasing specificity (highconfidence finance terms, moderate-confidence terms, and disambiguation terms used to distinguish between finance vs. accounting vs. marketing contexts). The Stage 2 XGBoost classifier was trained on 100K Stage-1-surviving documents 17 labeled by an LLM judge (prompted to apply binary finance vs. non-finance labels using detailed rubric); we used TF-IDF features with 50K-term vocabulary capped at unigrams and bigrams. The decision threshold was tuned on 5K-document held-out set to maximize F0.5 (precision-weighted). The lexicon files, the LLM-judge prompt, and the fitted TF-IDF vectorizer will be included in the public release.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.content: Structural prompt templates for RICoT and both baselines (task framing, stream-context format, and per-page decision schema) will be included in the public release; the verbatim instruction prose is withheld. All inference runs use temperature 0.001 and top-p 1; other sampling parameters are left at each providers defaults. Internal extended thinking is explicitly disabled in the RICoT runs and enabled in the baseline runs. Residual providerside nondeterminism is quantified in Appendix B.
